description: Prove your loops terminate and your branches branch: IF/CASE, LOOP/WHILE/FOR, and cursor lifecycle.

questions.explanation: The loop runs while v_count < 3: iterations make it 1, 2, 3 — then EXIT WHEN fires. Final value: 3.
No EXIT WHEN means no way out — this loop runs forever (or until someone kills the session). Every LOOP needs an exit condition.
options: Missing EXIT WHEN — this loops forever

questions.explanation: OPEN runs the query, FETCH grabs rows one at a time, %NOTFOUND tells you you're done, CLOSE releases the cursor. Always in that order.
questions.prompt: Put the cursor lifecycle in order.

questions.explanation: FOR i IN 1..5 runs exactly 5 times (1, 2, 3, 4, 5). No declaration of i needed, no exit needed — the range handles it.
questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: how many lines print?

questions.code:
v_tier := CASE
  WHEN v_points >= 1000 THEN 'gold'
  WHEN v_points >= 500 THEN 'silver'
  ___ 'bronze'
END;
questions.explanation: ELSE catches everything the WHENs didn't — here, points below 500. CASE always ends with END.
LOOP is manual, WHILE is conditional, FOR is counted, cursor is row-by-row. Pick the right tool for the repetition you need.
